ticket.title: Add [telemetry] enabled with env-wins precedence
ticket.description:
ADR 0012 decided telemetry is switched off at runtime, with precedence env -> config -> default(true). The env half exists (GAUGEBLOCK_NO_TELEMETRY, GB-340); this is the config half.

Add [telemetry] with an `enabled` key to .gaugeblock/config.toml and consult it in gaugeblock_workspace::telemetry::emission_enabled, so the check stays in the one choke point every emitter already goes through rather than being repeated per tool.

WHY THIS AND NOT A CARGO FEATURE, restated because it will be asked again: cargo features are additive. A downstream crate cannot switch one off - default-features = false only declines what the consumer would have enabled, and any other crate in the graph re-enables it. So a feature gate would look like an opt-out for exactly the case that motivates it (someone installing one tool) and would not be one. It would also save nothing: spans are contract types (ADR 0002), so uuid, serde and serde_json are already in the graph.

DEFAULT true, deliberately. The honest cost is a directory a panel-less user never reads, bounded by rotation (GB-341); the honest benefit is that first_diagnostic records what failed on a lone tool with no benchwork installed, which is a real use the panel does not cover.

TESTS: config false disables emission; env set disables emission even when config says true (precedence); absent config or absent key means enabled; and emission_enabled stays false in a test binary regardless of config, since GB-340 established that a test must not write the production log.

DEPENDS: GB-338 gives the writer one location, so the config is read from the same place it writes.

DONE 2026-11-08, and it uncovered a larger defect than the ticket described.

The switch itself: precedence is env -> `[telemetry] enabled` in `.gaugeblock/config.toml` -> default true. Config read
added as `SuiteConfig::boolean` returning Option<bool>, so absence is not false. `emission_enabled()` now composes
three conditions and the policy moved to its own module when telemetry.rs crossed 250 lines (3d9a856).

THE DEFECT: with `enabled = false` the log still grew. `SpanGuard::open` takes a path and writes, and
`InvocationSpan::start` called it directly, so the entire emission policy was inert on the only production path. That
includes GAUGEBLOCK_NO_TELEMETRY, which was documented as an opt-out and ignored by exactly the spans the suite is
observed through. The earlier test-binary proof was against sawhorse's own writer, not this one, which is why nothing
caught it. Fixed in a26f738 by consulting the policy at the entry point.

PROVEN, three runs against an installed binary:
  enabled = false          -> log unchanged (38 -> 38)
  enabled = true           -> log grew     (38 -> 39)
  GAUGEBLOCK_NO_TELEMETRY  -> log unchanged (39 -> 39)

WHY THIS WAS MISSED: the unit test proved the config parser, and the config parser worked. Nothing tested that opening
a span consults the policy at all. A feature that is correctly implemented and never called looks identical to one
that is called and broken, until something is run.

REGRESSION CHECKED 2026-11-08, after every other change of the day (the policy split, the entry-point guard, the chain

  [telemetry] enabled = true   -> storypole list + chalkline docs check grew the log 86 -> 88, both spans carrying

  [telemetry] enabled = false  -> the same two commands left the log at 88

So the switch does both jobs it was asked to do, and did not become a one-way valve while the surrounding code moved.
The config was left at `enabled = true`.

Worth doing because the guard now sits at the entry point of every span in the suite, and a bug there would have been
silent in the most expensive way: commands would run correctly, exit zero, and leave no record that they had - which is
indistinguishable from telemetry that was never wired, the exact ambiguity this epic spent its length removing.
